plain_english_policy: This bill establishes a legislative veto over any transfer of control—including leasing, transferring, or outsourcing management—to private (nongovernmental) entities for Alabama’s state-run mental health and developmental disability institutions. It requires explicit legislative approval via a supermajority vote (three-fifths in each chamber) before such transfers can occur.
policy_direction_if_enacted: The bill would shift power from the executive branch (the Department of Mental Health commissioner) to the legislature, creating a higher barrier for privatization or outsourcing of state mental health facilities. sponsorship_supports_position: The bill’s text and legislative referral (Government Appropriations committee) suggest sponsors prioritize **state control over mental health services**—likely to prevent privatization without legislative oversight.
evidence_quotes: An institution over which the department exercises control may not be leased, transferred, or placed under the supervision or management of any nongovernmental entity without first obtaining the consent of the Legislature through the passage of legislation by a three-fifths vote of the membership of each house.
